player_0.content: New plan: I incorrectly identified the sentence as ambiguous because I focused solely on the grammatical possibility of "his" referring to either Bailey or the director. However, in standard English usage, the pronoun "his" in the phrase "meet the director at his office" typically defaults to the subject of the main clause (Bailey) unless context suggests otherwise, making (B) the most likely intended answer rather than (C). Next time, I will apply pragmatic principles of default reference, assuming the pronoun refers to the subject (Bailey) unless there is explicit evidence to the contrary, and select option (B).
